Commentary.Commentary: So that's it from us for this game. We hope you enjoyed our coverage. We are not promoting four-day Tests but the sides on show probably did. Both were guilty of thinking too ahead too early and it cost Zimbabwe more than West Indies. The second Test begins on 29th October, 2017 at the same venue. Action begins at 1000 local (0800 GMT). We look forward to your company. Until then, it's goodbye and take care.

Man of the Match, Devendra Bishoo says he's quite happy as he got some wickets under his belt. Adds that the conditions in England made it difficult for him to get wickets, so is happy to do well here. States that it's just hard work that's got him here. When asked about missing out on his fifty, he says that he is disappointed to miss out on it and hopes that he won't make the same mistake next time.

Jason Holder says that they started well with the bat but lost their way in the middle. Reckons that it was a difficult wicket to bat on. Since it was tough to get a start here, he credits his bowlers who created pressure and got wickets. Opines that the track gripped a lot on the first day and then became slower as the game progressed. Lauds the contribution of the spinners from both sides and even the pacers, hoping that there is something for the latter in the next Test. Credits Bishoo for bowling well and even contributing with the bat and adds that he was unlucky to miss out on a deserving 50. He states that Brathwaite is an underrated bowler as he varies his flight and pace. He went with his gut feeling to hand the ball to him who gave them the first breakthrough. Ends wishing Ian Bishop a very happy birthday.

Graeme Cremer says they did really well on the first day getting the visitors out for 219, but then lost their way on the second with the bat. Applauds West Indies for batting well in their second innings. Admits they knew it was going to be tough. Credits Roston Chase and Devendra Bishoo for their bowling performances. Cites loss of concentration as the biggest factor for their defeat. Says that Solomon Mire did well on his debut and will come good eventually. Adds that Hamilton Masakadza has been great for them and he'll kick on soon enough. Opines his seamers did well on a tough bowling wicket and is also happy with the spin department, just wants to get more runs on the board. Mentions that as they play more Test cricket, they will get more familiar with the nature of the game and only get better.

The hosts needed to bat and apply themselves better in the first innings and it could have made a difference on this wicket which settled as the game went on. West Indies were down and out after the first day but showed tremendous character to bounce back and register the win. They will be pleased with the effort. Stay tuned for the presentation ceremony.

Zimbabwe began really well with both the openers Hamilton Masakadza and Solomon Mire going great guns. The 99-run opening stand had set it up well for them but as is the case on such wickets, one brings two and they lost four wickets in the second session today to be at the brink of a loss. Brendan Taylor was the lone man fighting for them with a valiant 73. Bishoo finished with nine wickets in the fixture and was easily the best bowler on display for the visitors. Ironically though it was the run out involving him and Waller that triggered a mini-collapse. Chris Mpofu and Kyle Jarvis had some fun for the last wicket but Graeme Cremer would know that they have missed a shot at history.

It was Devendra Bishoo who took a fifer to skittle out the home side for a meager 159, thereby helping his side gain a 60-run lead. The tourists didn't look back since then and batted the hosts out of the game. Kraigg Brathwaite, the Hope brothers and Roston Chase played vital knocks to set a mammoth target of 434 runs in front of the home side.

Brilliant comeback by West Indies to win this game and take a 1-0 lead in this 2-match Test series. They appeared to be a long way behind when they were bowled out for 219 in their first innings after winning the toss and batting. Only Kieran Powell and Shai Hope were the ones who put up a fight. They were brought back in the game by their bowlers.

The third umpire is involved now. Replays show that the batsman hasn't made it in and has to walk back. Taylor knew that he was short as seen from his reaction. A very good knock comes to an end now. The end is nigh.
What's happening there? It's all coming down for Zimbabwe. There is a run out appeal against Taylor. The third umpire is referred to. Chances of surviving look very bleak.

Drinks have been taken! And West Indies have regained control, if there was any point when they ever lost it. Brendan Taylor and Sikandar Raza were going along well but the latter's dismissal has tipped the scales in the visitor's favour again. From now on, it might just be a matter of when and not if, for West Indies to get over the finish line.

OUT! See that is why, I wrote on the previous ball that it was not a good ploy to have Raza facing Bishoo. He was troubling him in the last over. This time Bishoo bowls one around off, very short asking to be hit. What Raza manages to do is hit it straight to Chase at covers who takes a good catch diving to his right. That's a really vital wicket for the Windies and Bishoo is delighted. That is why Zimbabwe need to play more Test cricket to understand the value of making most of starts. Twice in the game, Raza has got out to poor shots at the wrong time. Not that there is a good time to get out but you have to make sure you do not give the opposition an inch. West Indies have an opening here, will they trigger a collapse from hereon? Zimbabwe still need 215 more runs to win.

Full and reversing into the batsman from around off, Taylor turns it through backward square leg for a couple.
In the air... but safe! Good length around off, Taylor looks to whip it but does so aerially towards short mid-wicket.

Roach goes wide of the crease and angles it on the stumps on a fuller length. Taylor is hit on his pads as he fails to clip it through. The players appeal but the umpire says no. Holder reckons there was an inside edge and replays show he was right. Nice start for Kemar.

We're back for the final session of play. 35 overs, 275 runs, 6 wickets - these are the numbers that matter for now. Zimbabwe were going really well at Lunch but lost their way to be in this position. They were playing their shots but have now gone into a shell. Will they return to playing their shots to survive or will we see some grit and determination? Sikandar Raza and Brendan Taylor come out to bat. West Indies begin with Kemar Roach. Here we go...
... Day 4, Session 3 ...

Zimbabwe slip further! Plain and simple. West Indies took 4 wickets and ran through the top order with the spinners doing most of the damage. The runs were never a bother for the visitors and with 275 still needed for the hosts to win, the task has become more monumental than ever. It's a long shot, but 6 wickets are still in hand, and Brendan Taylor is out there with Sikandar Raza. Their first objective will be to see out the day. Advantage Windies for now! Should be a good final phase of play. We'll be back shortly.
Bishoo serves this outside off, Raza opts to leave it alone. That's TEA, DAY4!
Drifting in first before turning away, Raza comes ahead and meets it with a straight bat.
Similar ball, knocked into the cover once more for nothing.
Full ball pitched outside off, some room on offer so Sikandar Raza plays the expansive drive. Connects well but is unfortunate he finds the man at cover.
Some air provided on this on off, Raza prods forward in defense.
Slower through the air on middle and off, Taylor makes time for himself by going back and works it to mid-wicket for a single.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Short again, kept out off the back foot.
Quicker, flatter and short outside off, Sikandar Raza off the back foot meets it with a firm punch through the covers for a couple of runs.
Looped up off spinner on off stump, it's swept fine down the leg side for an easy single.
Spinning in from around off, Brendan moves across his sticks, gets behind the line and defends.
Straighter one outside off, Brendan leans across to block it out.
Quite full again, a tight defensive shot from Sikandar Raza to end the over.
Full delivery on the stumps, driven down to mid on.

Ripper first up to Sikandar Raza! Almost had him there. Drops it on middle and off and it turns away heavily. Raza is squared up a bit as he attempts to defend off the back foot. Gets beaten past the outside edge as the keeper collects it.
Sikandar Raza walks into the middle next.

OUT! That's a tame dismissal, really. Should have done so much better there. But this is a huge breakthrough for Windies, Bishoo is continuing his heroics from the first innings. Slower through the air on middle and off, Williams is down the track to block but the ball sneaks past the inside edge, hits his pads and thuds into Dowrich's gloves. The keeper does really well to keep his eyes on the ball and whip the bails off. Williams does not even try getting back. It has been a poor Test for him, with the bat. Hang on though! This is interesting. Upon watching the replays, it's seen that there was a slight inside edge as well. So, maybe that's why he didn't really try to get back in his crease with any kind of urgency. Knew he was gone either way.
Bit more air on this outside off, Taylor with a drive through the covers for one.
Turning away from around off, beats the outside edge of Taylor's hanging bat as he looks to defend.
Back of a length outside off, punched off the back foot on the off side.

FOUR! That's gone away to the fence but Williams is not happy with himself. Wasn't exactly in control of the shot there. Fuller outside off, he drives it but uppishly over the cover fielders. It goes all the way but a player of his quality will know that's not good enough.
Marginally ahead of a length very close to the off stick, blocked out off the front foot.
Raymon Reifer is on the field for Shai Hope.
The ball is way outside the off stump, easy leave for the batsman.

On a length once more going across Williams, he plays this away from his body as he punches it through the covers. Chase gets to it from cover-point, fails to cut it off, hits Reifer's (sub) boot and goes towards point. Two runs taken.
Good length delivery angling across, Williams with a solid back foot punch to the extra cover fielder.
Transfers his weight onto his back foot and pushes it into the covers.
Fuller in length again, Brendan brings his bat ahead of his pad and keeps it out down the track.
Full and attacking the stumps, defended.
Lovely stuff from Bishoo! Tossed up on off, spins away with a puff of dust. Taylor prods forward to defend but is beaten past the outside edge.
Goes against the spin this time. It's a bit straighter in line which allows Taylor to turn it down to short fine leg.
Straighter one on middle and off, worked away past the vacant short leg region.
Cutting back in from a length around off, Williams hangs back inside his crease and sees it out safely.
Stays right behind the line of this one and keeps it out.
Bit full outside off, driven on up straight to the extra cover fielder.
Serves it on a good length in the off stump channel, left alone for the keeper to collect.
Angling back into the batsman on middle and off, Williams goes for the fluent drive but gets it off the inside edge and onto this pads.
Comes around the wicket and fires it full outside off, Williams drives it with the full face of the bat to mid off.
Floated outside off, Brendan Taylor covers the line and lets it be.

FOUR! Short delivery outside off, Taylor rocks onto his back foot and cracks it through the covers. Brathwaite gives it a long chase and slides just inside the rope to keep it out, but fails in his attempt to do so as he touches the rope while still having contact with the ball.
Turn and bounce for Devendra Bishoo! Lands it around off and it grips and shoots off the surface. Taylor initially thinks about having a poke at it but then withdraws from the shot.
Quicker one just around off, spinning away a shade, Taylor goes deep inside his crease to block.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Extremely full on off stump, driven towards short extra cover where the fielder cuts it off.
A delivery which is fullish in length from Holder, Sean Williams ends the over by blocking it out off the front foot.
Fires it in full on middle and leg, Taylor with another flick through square leg for one more.
Too straight in line once more, Brendan Taylor flicks it behind square leg and takes two as the man in the deep mops it up.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Going down leg once more, no trouble for the batsman to leave it alone.
Short ball angling down the leg side, ducked and evaded.
Sean Williams is the next batsman in. He wasn't quite himself in the first innings and will want to change that this time around.

OUT! He's gone! That's a big wicket for Windies, Bishoo with a vital breakthrough. He floats it up nicely on the stumps, skids on and keeps a little low as well. Craig Ervine goes back to flick but is beaten by the lack of turn and struck on the pads. Loud shout and the umpire raises his finger after a thought. Ervine thinks he's gone, he confers with Taylor who tells him to review it. It's taken upstairs and replays show that he's gone on all counts. Zimbabwe lose their third, Windies right on top here.
Is he gone? Bishoo gets Ervine LBW. After some discussion with Taylor, the batsman decides to opt for the review.
It's pitched too full so it doesn't spin much, Brendan drives it down to long off for a single.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Short and flat outside off, punched just wide of the mid off fielder for a run.
Looped up leg spinner outside off, Taylor plays with the spin and drives it through the covers for a single.
Flighted around off, Ervine with a little shimmy down the track takes it on the full and hits it down to long on for one.
Goes a bit fuller this time on off stump, met with a straight blade in defense.
Leg gully in place now.
Bit shortish in length outside off, kept out well off the back foot.
Angling down the leg side, Taylor attempts to tickle it fine down leg but misses.
Outside off on a good length, no shot offered by the batsman.

FOUR! Lovely innovation from Brendan Taylor! Short ball on middle and leg, he crouches low at first to leave it but then at the last second, plays the upper cut over the keeper's head to send it across the fine leg boundary. Ingenious! It's a delight to watch how he manufactures his shots and scores his runs.
Back of a length delivery cutting back in from around off, Taylor walks a step across to cover the line and shoulders arms to it.
FOUR! That's a gift from Bishoo! Juicy full toss outside off, Ervine accepts it and crashes it through the gap in the covers for a boundary.
Easily done. Knocks this full ball down to long off for a single.
Nice loop on this from Bishoo, Taylor gets very close to the pitch of the ball to stop it from spinning and smothers it in its tracks.
Tosses it right up there on off stump, Brendan is well forward in defense.
Closer to the off stick this time, kept out well from inside the crease.
Drops it short to begin with, well outside off and it turns a long way. Taylor reaches out to it and hits it to the man at cover.
Devendra Bishoo is into the attack now.
Too straight in line again, nudged behind square leg for a comfortable run.
Shout for a leg before, turned down. Was always going down leg, no chance for it to be given out. Fuller ball angling down on leg, catches Brendan Taylor on the pads as he misses his attempted flick.
Full length delivery around off, moving away at the last second, Taylor is still behind the line of the ball as he defends it.
Reversing back into the batsman from outside off, on a fullish length, Taylor plants his front foot forward and meets it with the full face of the bat.
Shaping back in on middle and leg, tucked away to the backward square leg fielder.
Short of a good length outside off, rising off the deck a bit as Brendan Taylor gets on his toes to block. Takes it on the gloves as the ball falls down on the ground.
Fullish in length attacking the stumps, blocked.
Darted well outside off, Craig with an easy leave to make.
Looped up from around the wicket to Ervine, he prods forward and guards it out.
Full again on the stumps, eased in front of mid on for a quick single.
Full on middle and leg, works it on the leg side for nothing.
Flat and short outside off, Ervine off the back foot punches it to covers. Both batsmen run hard and eventually the throw at the striker's end is beaten.
This delivery is played to the man at mid-wicket.
Shorter length on the stumps, Taylor gets on his toes and clips it towards backward square leg.
Bouncer around off, Taylor crouches low and sways away from the line to let it go.
Holder lands it on the stumps, Brendan drives it towards mid on.
Back of a length around off, Taylor stands tall and pushes it towards gully. Signals to his partner to not come for a run.
Bowled fuller around off and middle, flicked straight to the man stationed at mid-wicket.
Jason Holder is back on. 6-0-16-0 read his current figures. A slip and a gully in place.

Drinks are on the field now. Windies will be happy with the two wickets. The openers for the home side were going strong before Brathwaite provided his side with the breakthrough. As often is the case, another one followed in quick succession as Roach too joined the party. Taylor and Ervine should use their experience to steer Zimbabwe to safety at least till the next break. It is going to require a hard grind from both of them as the ball is beginning to reverse a touch as well.
Served around off and middle, Taylor flicks it past short leg for one run.
Ervine goes back and pulls it towards wide mid on for a run.
Bowled around off, Ervine defends it by getting nicely forward.
Served in line of the stumps, Taylor taps it to the on side. The ball bounces over the short leg fielder and the batsmen rotate the strike.
Flatter around off, Brendan goes back and tucks it in front of square on the leg side for a brace.
Tossed up around off, Taylor lunges forward to defend.
Pitched up to the batsman in line of the off stump, Ervine drives it to the mid off region.
Roach comes round the wicket and bowls it around off. Ervine stays in the crease and presents a straight bat to block it.
Fuller delivery around off and middle, Taylor clips it to the fielder at deep mid-wicket for one run.
Hurled outside off, Brendan drives it straight to the cover fielder.
Angled into the batsman around off and middle, Taylor gets it off the inner half towards mid-wicket.
Kemar runs in and sprays this full down the leg side. Taylor looks to flick but misses.
Ervine lunges forward and blocks it with a straight bat.
FOUR! Ervine plays across the line successfully! Brathwaite loops it around off, Craig just plays it with a cross bat through mid-wicket for a boundary.
Fuller outside off, driven towards mid off.
Served outside off, Craig looks to cut it but misses.
Flatter on the pads, Taylor misses the flick and the ball takes his thigh pad and goes past leg slip. A leg bye taken.
Flighted around off, Taylor hits it towards mid-wicket.
Another ball well outside off, left alone.
Landed wide of off, Craig covers his stumps and lets it pass to the keeper.
Spears it around off, Ervine presents a straight bat as he defends.
Hurled full outside off, Ervine doesn't bother playing with that.

Kemar Roach is adopting an approach similar to that of the Zimbabwe bowlers - he is bowling full and on the middle and leg stump. They failed as the Windies batters are good with their on-side play but the hosts' batsmen seem to struggle with that. We could see Mire being dismissed with the same kind of ball and even in the previous over bowled by Kemar, Taylor wasn't overtly comfortable. So it's a good ploy by the tourists here.
Bowled on the pads, tucked away comfortably to fine leg for a run.
Hurled around off, Taylor presents with the full face of the bat as he defends.
Bowled around off, driven towards mid off.
Craig gets nicely forward and buries it on the ground.
FOUR! Lovely shot! That just raced away to the fence. Brathwaite floats it outside off, Ervine gets forward and just times the push through covers perfectly and gets a boundary.
Similar delivery, Craig blocks it with a straight bat.
Dropped full around off, Ervine strides forward and blocks it.
Served around off, Ervine pushes it towards covers.
Pitched further up around off, Taylor drives it to the fielder at mid off.
Hurled around off, Taylor pushes it towards mid off.
Fuller around middle and leg, Taylor clips it towards square leg.
On a length outside off, Brendan shoulders arms to let it be.
Another lovely yorker angled in to the batsman. Taylor does well to keep it out towards mid-wicket.
Fuller around off, Taylor pushes it back towards the bowler.
Another delivery outside off, Ervine lets it be.
Flatter on the pads, Ervine misses the flick and gets hit on the pads.
Landed outside off, Craig doesn't bother playing that.
Well bowled. Brathwaite floats it outside off, Ervine is drawn forward but the ball spins away to beat the edge of the bat.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Flatter outside off, Ervine covers the stumps and lets it go.

Shane Dowrich is next in line to feel the heat it seems. They physio is out to have a look at him. Is it dehydration? He's having his face looked at, maybe there's a cut somewhere around his eyebrow? Not sure. Either way, he's fine and ready to continue.
Brendan Taylor walks in next for the hosts. He needs to play a responsible knock to keep his side in the game. Remember, they have got a good start as of now.

OUT! One brings two! Roach hurls it full around off that tails in even more after pitching. Mire gets overbalanced as he looks to jam it out. Misses the ball completely and it strikes his back pad and disturbs the stumps. Solomon was looking fidgety for sometime now and this is a very untimely dismissal for the hosts. He has played well but the visitors are ecstatic as both the set batsmen are gone now.
This ball is well kept out off the front foot with a straight bat.

Ian Bishop makes a valid point on air after Masakadza's dismissal. He observes that the reason for the bat-pad dismissal was the bat being besides the pad and not in front of it. This makes the batter vulnerable to get an inside edge as well as a chance of being out LBW.

FOUR! Streaky runs for Mire these! Roach bowls it on a length around off, Solomon looks to punch it off the back foot. Gets a thick outside edge that races away through the vacant slip region for another boundary.
Mire pushes it towards mid-wicket.
Landed around off, blocked off the front foot onto the ground.
FOUR! Cleverly played! Back of a length delivery outside off, Mire stays back and looks to guide it towards third man. Gets a thick edge through the vacant slip cordon for a boundary.
Kemar Roach is brought back to bowl. Holder senses an opportunity to create pressure and stifle the opposition and hence he has brought his strike bowler back.
Floated on the stumps, Ervine clips it away through mid-wicket for a brace to get off the mark. Brings up the 100 for the hosts as well.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Served on a fuller length in line of the stumps, Craig bunts it with a straight bat.
Landed around off, Ervine blocks it from the crease.
Craig Ervine is in at No.3. He walks into the middle with a solid platform laid for him. He'll be vital for Zimbabwe's chances in this game.

OUT! Brathwaite strikes! Yes, of all the bowlers, he gives Windies the crucial breakthrough and Masakadza cannot believe what has just happened. Floated around off, Hamilton lunges forward in defense. The ball spins in, takes the inside edge, lobs off his pads and lands into the safe hands of Shai Hope at short leg. That's the end of a very good knock from the senior opener but he would be ruing the fact that he couldn't carry on. The 99-run stand is broken now and the visitors would look to make further strikes.
Flatter on the stumps, Masakadza stays back and blocks it.
Shannon lands this on the pads, Masakadza nurdles it towards fine leg for a single. 7 runs came off it.
Speared outside off, Hamilton drives it through covers. Beats the man who dives there and gets a brace.

FOUR! Overpitched, punished! Gabriel bowls it outside off, Masakadza gets the opportunity to free his arms and he does so. Goes for the drive but gets it off the outer half of his bat through backward point for a boundary.
Bowled around off, the batter stays put and blocks it from the crease.
On a length outside off, Masakadza just lets it be and shoulders arms to that.
Hurled around off, Hamilton drives it towards mid off.
Mire, calm down! This isn't needed. Looks to reverse sweep against the turn and the ball spins down just past the leg stump.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Bowled in line of the stumps, Mire gets forward to block.

What happened there? Brathwaite fires it short around off and middle, Mire goes back to pull it. Gets a bottom edge onto his pads that lobs up towards short leg. The fielder there, in reaction to the attempted shot, ducks and hence doesn't have his eyes on the ball. He couldn't react to a possible catch that he had to his left. Mire is lucky there.
Mire looks to reverse sweep but gets it off his gloves towards leg slip.

7th Test fifty for Hamilton Masakadza! It has been a sensible and disciplined knock from him. Zimbabwe needed a good start in pursuit of a big total and the senior pro has stood up. Brathwaite floats it around off, the batter drives it down to long on for a run.
Full toss outside off, driven towards mid off by the batsman.
Top shot! Full and outside off, Mire gets right forward and creams it drive past the diving Holder at mid off for a couple of runs.
Full and outside off, driven towards mid off by the batsman.
Similar line, turned through mid-wicket for a single.

NOT OUT! What a waste of a review! Gabriel hurls it around leg, Masakadza looks to defend it from his crease with his bat and pad together. The players appeal as the ball strikes the pad but the umpire says no. Gabriel is convinced and hence Holder goes for the review. Does not look a good review to the naked eye. Ball Tracker shows the same and West Indies have blown a review here. Replays show that Dowrich did indicate that it was probably going down leg but Jason still went for the review. He has a history of wasting them.
Angles it outside off, left alone by Mire. The keeper fumbles and gets a bye.
Masakadza gets in line and defends it.
FOUR! This time Masakadza gets a boundary with a reverse sweep! Similar ball, Hamilton unfurls a lovely reverse sweep to the third man fence. Superb shot, that.
Shorter outside off, defended watchfully off the back foot.

Hamilton Masakadza has played many pull shots since this morning. What is good to note is that he has a forward press before transferring his weight back. This helps him pick the length early and execute his shots better.
Lands it outside off again, played back to the bowler.
Fuller around off, Masakadza comes forward and defends it.
Good shot! Lands it outside off, Mire gets in position early and reverse sweeps it through backward point. Blackwood gives it a chase from first slip and saves a run for his side.
Interesting! Not Kemar Roach or Jason Holder, Kraigg Brathwaite to bowl after lunch. Very weird choice of bowler.
Angles it around middle, turned towards mid-wicket.
FOUR! Thumped! Full and outside off, Masakadza takes a stride forward and crashes it through covers for a majestic boundary. No second thoughts on this one.
Low full toss outside off, driven towards covers.
Fuller outside off, Hamilton wants to play at first but then thinks otherwise. The ball goes off the face of the bat towards point. Not ideal from Masakadza.
Fuller in length around off, comes in late, Masakadza aims to keep it out but gets an inside edge onto his pads. Replays confirm the same as Gabriel has his hands on his head.
Good length outside off, left alone by Masakadza.

Zimbabwe have begun well but how long can they carry the good work? The hosts will hope for long enough. Out come Hamilton Masakadza and Solomon Mire to bat. West Indies begin the session with Shannon Gabriel. He has a wide slip in place for him to stop the runs down to third man. Here we go...
... Day 4, Session 2 ...

West Indies were not bad but provided too many bad balls. They though will know that on such tracks, one wicket can lead to two and hence they won't be too disheartened. With a lot at stake, expect both sides to keep fighting. Let's see who takes the honors in the second session. Join us in a while for it.

Fantastic session of Test cricket for Zimbabwe. They first bowled out the tourists without conceding virtually anything and then their openers have done remarkably well to go into the first break unscathed. Both Hamilton Masakadza and Solomon Mire have played every ball on its merit and it has helped them build this stand. Yes, they still need 358 runs to win and it is still a long way away, but cricket is a game of glorious uncertainties and the hosts are on the right path for now.
Tossed up around off, Mire comes down and flicks it. The fielder at leg slip dives full stretch to his left to prevent any run. That's LUNCH, DAY 4!
This ball is played towards long off for one run.
Hamilton has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Masakadza gets nicely forward and defends it with a straight bat.
Mire dishes out the sweep shot and collects a run after the ball rolls through mid-wicket.
Begins with a delivery on the pads, Mire fails to flick it away and gets hit on the pads.
Kraigg Brathwaite comes into the attack now.
Driven through mid on by the batsman. They pick up a single.
This delivery is turned to mid-wicket.
Floated around off, Mire lunges forward and blocks.
This ball is flicked through square leg for a single.
Turn for Roston! Bowls it around off and middle, the ball spins down the leg side. Masakadza looks to flick but misses. The keeper misses and the ball rolls to short fine leg.
Chase is welcomed into the attack with a lovely shot. He loops it outside off, Mire drives it through covers. Roach chases it down and saves a run for his side.
Roston Chase is into the attack.
Landed outside off, Masakadza looks to cut but misses.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
In line of the stumps, Hamilton pushes it back towards the bowler.
Mire sweeps it towards deep mid-wicket for a single.

Ian Bishop on-air opines that he is not really in favour of the Kookaburra ball and prefers the Duke ball. He reasons that the latter has more chance of reversing when it gets old, which is more helpful to the bowlers.
Punched off the back foot by the batsman.
Flatter outside off, Mire allows it to spin away and lets it go.
This ball is outside off, Masakadza lets it go to the keeper.
Shorter length again, Hamilton pulls it towards mid-wicket.
Short around off, pulled away to deep mid-wicket for one run.
Bowled fuller on the stumps, defended off the front foot.
Length delivery, Mire defends it from the crease.
Length delivery outside off, Mire looks to play it towards third man but misses. He's done this twice now. Really needs to calm down and see off the non-run phase of play.
The batsman tried to sweep that one but missed it and was hit on the pads.
Another delivery outside off, left alone by the batter.
Served outside off, left alone by Hamilton.
Masakadza goes back and cuts it away towards point.
Bowled around off, driven towards covers.

Huge appeal! Bishoo floats it in line of the stumps, Masakadza lunges forward to defend but gets a slight inside edge onto his pads. The players appeal but don't get the nod. Replays confirm the presence of the inside edge.
This ball is flicked away through square leg for a run.
Mire drives it towards mid on and hares over to the other end.
Solomon gets forward to block this off the front foot.
Bowled straight on the stumps, Mire drives it towards mid on.

Holder would be a bit concerned. The Zimbabwe openers are attacking his main spin weapon Bishoo and countering his turn with sweeps. What does he do next then? Give Chase a go with the ball? Brathwaite may be? Or pacers from both ends?
Mire looks to defend this but gets an inside edge onto his pads.
Hurled on a length outside off, Mire has a feel for it but misses.
FOUR! Masakadza is looking good here! Floated around off, he gets his stride and gets low to sweep it through deep mid-wicket for a boundary.
Floated around off, Hamilton lunges forward but misses the ball as it spins away.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Masakadza gets nicely forward to defend that.
Bowled outside off, Hamilton doesn't bother playing that.
FOUR! Bashed! Bishoo serves it a tad short, Masakadza dismisses it from his presence. He goes back and pulls it over mid-wicket for a boundary.
This delivery is flicked towards mid-wicket.
Fuller around off, Solomon looks to drive but gets an inside edge onto the pads.
On a length outside off, Mire fishes at that but misses. Needs to careful here. Masakadza has a word with his partner immediately to calm him down.
Landed around off and middle, turned towards mid-wicket.

Very full delivery outside off, Mire fails to dig it out. There is an appeal made by Windies but nothing from the umpire. Holder wants to review it and looks around for an iota of support. Does not get it and hence does not go for the review. Replays show that the sound was of the bat hitting the ground and there was no contact with the ball.
Holder continues to bowl short, Mire continues to pull. Mistimes it straight to mid-wicket.
Looped outside off, arms are shouldered by Hamilton.
Landed around off, punched towards covers.
This ball is hit back straight to where it came from.

FOUR! The Zimbabweans are on a boundary-hitting spree at the moment. Bishoo serves it a tad short around middle, Masakadza allows the ball to spin as he goes back and pulls it through mid-wicket. Powell chases it valiantly but dives with the ball into the ropes.
Flatter on off, Mire goes back and punches it towards covers for a run.

FOUR! Now his partner's confidence is rubbing off on Mire! Bishoo floats it around off, Solomon nails the sweep. Plays it in front of square on the on side for a boundary. 50 runs up in style for the hosts!
FOUR! Too much of something is always harmful. Holder is learning it the hard way. Bowled around off, Masakadza pulls it powerfully through square leg for a boundary.
Fuller around off and middle, Masakadza mistimes his straight drive.
Holder bowls another short delivery around off, Hamilton pulls it through square leg for a brace.
Good running. Delivered on a back of a length around off, Masakadza stays tall and pulls it through backward square leg. Before the fine leg fielder gets there, a couple of runs result.
Shorter outside off, Masakadza looks to pull it but gets a bottom edge towards the off side.
Short ball around off, Mire mistimes his pull towards deep mid-wicket for a run. He got it off the splice of the bat.
This is bowled outside off, left alone by Hamilton.
Looped up around off and middle, Masakadza displays the forward defense to the T.
Now Hamilton is overdoing the sweep stroke. He looks to play that shot yet again but gets a bottom edge that goes on the bounce to the keeper.
Looped outside off, Hamilton looks to lunge forward and block but the ball spins away.
Masakadza tries to play the sweep now to a loopy ball outside off. Misses the ball completely.
Floated on the stumps, Mire gets down and sweeps it through backward square leg for a run.
Length delivery outside off, Masakadza punches it towards covers. He shouts a big NO to his partner.
Angled in to the batsman, he flicks it to mid-wicket.
Bowled full outside off, Masakadza strides forward and keeps it out watchfully.
Full outside off, driven towards covers.
Similar delivery and action sequence of the previous delivery.
Hurled around off, Hamilton strides forward to defend watchfully.
Punched off the back foot towards covers.
Served in line of the stumps, Solomon lunges forward to block it.
Floated outside off, Mire leaves it alone.
The batsman rocks onto the backfoot and punches the ball.

Hilarious! Bishoo loops it up around off, Mire gets down to paddle it. Blackwood runs to his left from first slip in anticipation of a catch. The batsman misses the ball completely and so does the keeper. The ball goes through where slip was originally standing. Two byes taken in the meanwhile.
Turn straightaway! Bishoo lands it around off, Mire strides forward to defend but the ball just spins past the edge of his bat.
Devendra Bishoo comes in to have a bowl. Would be interesting to see what he can extract from this surface. He has a slip in place. Also, it would be good to see how Mire approaches him.

Drinks have been taken! Zimbabwe have begun well in pursuit of a tall run chase. Not that Windies would mind it immediately as they have a lot of runs in the bank. But they would be wary of the fact that it could get difficult to displace batters once they are set.
This ball is blocked off the front foot onto the ground.

What's that? Overconfidence due to the boundary off the previous ball? Length delivery outside off, Masakadza has a wild slash at it without any foot movement. The ball passes close to the edge of the bat.
FOUR! Almost a catch! Holder lands it fuller around off, Masakadza drives it on the up straight back. The ball passes from the left of the bowler and races away to the boundary.
Fuller delivery around off, driven towards mid off.
Well bowled. Bowled on a length around off, the ball nips away after pitching. Masakadza plays for the initial angle but misses the ball after it moves away.
Begins with a length delivery around off and middle, Masakadza strides forward and blocks it right below his eyes.

Jason Holder brings himself into the attack. We have seen that he picks up crucial wickets against the run of play and it would be interesting to see how he goes about with his thing. A deep silly mid on to start with for him. Also a mid-wicket is in place.
On a length around off, Mire stands tall and chops it next to the stumps.
Bowled around off and middle, pushed towards mid on.

Should Jason Holder think of a third man? There have already been three boundaries in that particular area. They have a lot of runs on the board, so it should be interesting to see from when Holder starts to think about saving runs.
Gabriel bowls it outside off at 142 kmph, Mire shoulders arms to that. That was rather quick by Shannon yet it did not carry to the keeper. Shows the unevenness of the wicket.
This ball is bowled around off and middle, Mire gets behind the line of the ball and pushes it down the ground.

FOUR! Mire, in the first innings was all about the ravish strokes, here he is about the deft touches and pristine timing. Hurled fuller outside off, he watches it well and guides it through the gully region and earns himself a boundary.
Straight as an arrow! Fuller around off, Mire looks to push it from the crease and does so aerially straight back. The ball knocks back the stumps at the bowler's end.
Kemar is straying on the pads a bit too often. Does so again, Solomon clips it towards deep mid-wicket for a run. He wants a second but his partner shows no interest.

FOUR! A well-timed shot but fraught with danger. Roach hurls it full around middle, in spite of a mid-wicket being there, Mire flicks it off his pads. The ball goes aerially past the fielder there and races away to the fence.
This ball is blocked by presenting it with a straight bat.
FOUR! Cleverly played! On a length outside off, this bounced a tad more. Mire watches that carefully and cuts it through the gap between the gully and the second slip for a boundary.
There is the pitch showing its tricks. Roach bowls this with a straight seam on a length outside off. The ball refuses to get up and passes under Mire's bat and goes on the bounce to the keeper.
Roach delivers it full outside off from wide of the crease, Mire meets the ball with a full face of the bat and strokes it through covers. Gets two runs as a result.
Landed around off, the Zimbabwe opener gets behind it and pushes it with a straight bat towards covers.
Speared outside off, Hamilton is least bothered about playing that and shoulders arms in response.
Bowled outside off, Hamilton just lets it be and lets the keeper do the rest.
Fuller outside off, Masakadza gets it off the inner half towards the right of mid on. There could have been a quick run but the batters were a touch late to realise that.
Hurled full outside off, Hamilton covers his stumps and shoulders arms.
Very full delivery outside off, Hamilton stays in the crease and digs it out towards the bowler.
Another slower delivery outside off, Mire points his bat skywards and lets it go. The ball rolls away towards the keeper.
On a length outside off, Mire pushes it towards point.
Landed around off, the batsman defends it by getting behind the line of the ball.
Roach attempts to bowl a slower delivery but dishes out a low full toss. Solomon stays in the crease and keeps it out towards cover-point.
Fuller around off, driven towards mid off.
Hurled in line of the stumps, Mire gets behind the line and pushes it towards mid on.

FOUR! Streaky! On a length around off, Masakadza strides forward to defend but gets a thick outside edge. The ball goes through the gap between the slip and the gully fielder and it goes away to the fence.
One slip goes out now.
A slower leg cutter outside off, Masakadza doesn't bother playing that and lets it be.
Bowled outside off, Hamilton strides forward and drives it through covers for a brace.
Fuller around off, Masakadza is stuck in the crease and he gets an inside edge onto his pads as he looks to defend.

FOUR! Authoritative and confident stroke! Gabriel bangs this short around off that climbs up chest high. Masakadza doesn't mind if there is a fielder in the deep or not. He pulls it in front of square on the leg side and beats the fielder in the deep comfortably as he collects his first boundary.
Bowled around off, Hamilton stays in the crease and defends it with a straight bat.

Mid-wicket now drops back for Masakadza. There are a couple of slips and a deep gully in place as well. This surely will keep the batsman guessing as to whether it will be a fuller delivery or a shorter one.
Jason Holder is seen taking a couple of tablets. The heat might already be getting to him it seems.
Mire shows the full face of the bat and defends it off the front foot.
Full outside off, driven nicely towards covers.
This delivery is nudged in front of square on the leg side for a run.

Beautiful bowling. Roach runs in and hurls it on a length outside off. Masakadza strides forward to defend but misses. The ball passes the edge of the bat and goes to the keeper. There is a stifled appeal to no avail. There was a sound and it was of the bat hitting the pad. The bowler had delivered it with a straight seam, as seen from the replays, and that meant that the ball held its line and went through.
This delivery is driven to the fielder at covers.
Lovely looking shot. Fuller around off and middle, Masakadza drives it back down the ground. Mid on comes there to cut it off.
FOUR! Change of plan for Gabriel. He goes to his strength and bowls it short around off. Mire is quick to respond and pulls it away aerially in front of square. The ball goes away to the fence.
Gabriel is searching for the swing as well and bowls it fuller around off, Solomon knocks it towards covers from the crease.
Hurled outside off, Mire doesn't bother playing that.
On the shorter side, Mire stands tall and taps it towards cover-point.

It would be interesting to see Solomon Mire's approach here. In the first innings, he looked aggressive from the onset. Will he do so again? Or would the mountain of runs in front of him make him alter his game?
Length ball around off, pushed towards mid off from the crease.
Gabriel runs in and hurls it fuller around off, Mire pushes it off the front foot towards mid on.
Shannon Gabriel will steam in with the new ball from the other end.
On a length around off, Masakadza defensively pushes it towards covers.
Speared on the stumps, the opener stands tall and pushes it back towards the bowler.
Bowled around middle, Masakadza drives it down towards mid on.
Kemar Roach is getting some inswing there. He spears this full again, Hamilton flicks it towards mid-wicket.
Roach hurls this full around middle and leg, the batsman flicks it away through square leg for a brace.
Roach steams in and spears it full on the pads, Masakadza looks to flick but misses. Gets hit low on the pads.
